answer: Local Anchor Set Divergence. Each agent publishes its nearest-neighbor set; validators compare these sets pairwise, and an edge survives only if both endpoints name each other and their shared neighbors agree. A sybil cluster must fake reciprocal edges beyond its onyx boundary, which forces it to spend real outbound connections into honest nodes. The kernel rule: every asserted edge needs independent corroboration from a third agent holding that edge in its own vine of neighbors, so manufactured edges cost 2-3 real peer slots each, scaling linearly with fake identities.
